info.title: Key Manager API
info.description:
Scaleway Key Manager allows you to create, manage, and use cryptographic keys in a centralized and secure service. All your cryptographic operations can be delegated to Key Manager, which in turn ensures the security and availability of your keys.

Key Manager supports the following cryptographic operations: data encryption, data decryption, and data encryption key generation.

## Concepts

Refer to our [dedicated concepts page](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/key-manager/concepts/) to learn about the different concepts and terms related to Key Manager.

## Quickstart

<Message type="requirement">
 - You have a [Scaleway account](https://console.scaleway.com/)
 - You have your [Organization and your Project ID](https://console.scaleway.com/project/settings)
 - You have created an [API key](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/iam/how-to/create-api-keys/) and the API key has sufficient [IAM permissions](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/iam/reference-content/permission-sets/) to perform the actions described on this page
 - You have [installed `curl`](https://curl.se/download.html)
</Message>

1. **Configure your environment variables.**

   <Message type="note">
   This is an optional step that aims to simplify your usage of the API.
   </Message>

    ```bash
    export SCW_ACCESS_KEY="<API access key>"
    export SCW_SECRET_KEY="<API secret key>"
    export SCW_PROJECT_ID="<Scaleway Project ID>"
    ```

2. **Create a key**. Run the following command to create a key that you can use to encrypt and decrypt your data:

    ```bash
    curl "https://api.scaleway.com/key-manager/v1alpha1/regions/$REGION/keys" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -H "X-Auth-Token: $SCW_SECRET_KEY" \
      -d '{
        "project_id": "$PROJECT_ID",
        "name": "my-key",
        "usage": {
            "symmetric_encryption": "aes_256_gcm"
        }
       }'
    ```

3. **Rotate your key**. Run the following command to generate a new version of your key. This operation renders your previous key version obsolete.

    ```bash
    curl "https://api.scaleway.com/key-manager/v1alpha1/regions/$REGION/keys/<KEY_ID>/rotate" \
      -H "X-Auth-Token: $SCW_SECRET_KEY" \
      -d '{
        "key_id": "$KEY_ID"
      }'
    ```

4. **Encrypt data**. Run the following command to encrypt data with the key you have created in step 2:

    ```bash
    curl "https://api.scaleway.com/key-manager/v1alpha1/regions/$REGION/keys/<KEY_ID>/encrypt" \
      -H "X-Auth-Token: $SCW_SECRET_KEY" \
      -d '{
        "key_id": "$KEY_ID",
        "plaintext": "'"$(echo -n "plaintext-data" | base64)"'"
      }'
    ```

5. **Generate a data encryption key**. Run the following command to generate a data encryption key that you can use for cryptographic operations outside of Key Manager:

    ```bash
    curl "https://api.scaleway.com/key-manager/v1alpha1/regions/$REGION/keys/<KEY_ID>/generate-data-key" \
      -H "X-Auth-Token: $SCW_SECRET_KEY" \
      -d '{
        "key_id": "$KEY_ID",
        "algorithm": "aes_256_gcm"
      }'
    ```

## Technical information

### Regions

Scaleway's infrastructure spans different [regions and Availability Zones](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/account/reference-content/products-availability/).

Key Manager is available in all regions.

## Technical limitations

- While Scaleway Key Manager is responsible for generating, encrypting, and decrypting [data encryption keys](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/key-manager/concepts/#data-encryption-key-dek/), it does not store, manage, or monitor them, nor does it engage in cryptographic operations with these keys. **You must use and manage data encryption keys outside of Key Manager**. Read our [security recommendations](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/key-manager/reference-content/security-recommendations/) to find out about security measures to be aware of while using Key Manager.

### Symmetric encryption

- The maximum payload size that can be encrypted is 64 KB of plaintext.
- The maximum payload size that can be decrypted is around 131 KB of data.
- The only symmetric algorithm currently supported by Key Manager is AES-256-GCM.

### Asymmetric encryption

Key Manager supports the following asymmetric encryption algorithms:

- RSA-OAEP-2048-SHA256
- RSA-OAEP-3072-SHA256
- RSA-OAEP-4096-SHA256

### Asymmetric signing

Key Manager supports the following asymmetric signing algorithms:

- EC-P256-SHA256
- EC-P384-SHA384
- RSA-PSS-2048-SHA256
- RSA-PSS-3072-SHA256
- RSA-PSS-4096-SHA256
- RSA-PKCS1-2048-SHA256
- RSA-PKCS1-3072-SHA256
- RSA-PKCS1-4096-SHA256
- ML-DSA-44
- ML-DSA-65
- ML-DSA-87

For ECDSA and RSA keys, the `digest` is 32 bytes (SHA-256) or 48 bytes (SHA-384).

For ML-DSA keys in `raw` mode, the message can be between 1 and 4096 bytes.

For ML-DSA keys in `external_mu` mode, the pre-hashed μ message representative must be exactly 64 bytes.

### Key Encapsulation

Key Manager supports the following key encapsulation algorithms:

- MLKEM-768
- MLKEM-1024

## Going further

For more information about Key Manager, you can check out the following pages:

- [Key Manager documentation](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/key-manager/)
- [Contact our Support team](https://console.scaleway.com/support/tickets).

tags.name: Keys
tags.description: Keys are logical containers you create in Key Manager to store cryptographic keys. They support encryption, decryption, and the generation of data encryption keys.

key_id.description: ID of the data encryption key. (UUID format)

algorithm.description: Symmetric encryption algorithm of the data encryption key (`AES-256-GCM`).

ciphertext.description:
Data encryption key ciphertext.
Your data encryption key's ciphertext can be stored safely. It can only be decrypted through the keys you create in Key Manager, using the relevant key ID.

plaintext.description:
Data encryption key plaintext.
(Optional) Your data encryption key's plaintext allows you to use the key immediately upon creation. It must neither be stored or shared.

created_at.description: Data encryption key creation date. (RFC 3339 format)

values.aes_256_gcm: Key Manager currently only supports the `AES-GCM` (256-bits) data key algorithm.

key_id.description: ID of the key used for decryption. (UUID format)

ciphertext.description:
(Optional) Data encrypted with the latest key rotation.
If the data was already encrypted with the latest key rotation, no output will be returned in the response object.

key_id.description: ID of the key used for encryption. (UUID format)
ID of the target key. (UUID format)

public_key.description: The public key to wrap the key material.

import_token.description: The token generated to authorize the import operation.

data.description:
The encrypted key material to import.
This material must be encrypted using the public key and the exact wrapping algorithm returned by the `GetKeyMaterialImportParameters` method.

import_token.description: The secure import token returned by the `GetKeyMaterialImportParameters` method.

project_id.description: ID of the Project containing the key. (UUID format)

usage.description:
Key usage.
See the `Key.Usage` enum for a description of possible values.

state.description:
Key state.
See the `Key.State` enum for a description of possible values.

rotation_count.description:
Number of key rotations.
The rotation count tracks the number of times the key has been rotated.

protected.description: Returns `true` if key protection is applied to the key.

locked.description: Returns `true` if the key is locked.

origin.description:
Key origin.
Refer to the `Key.Origin` enum for a description of values.

deletion_requested_at.description: Returns the time at which deletion was requested. (RFC 3339 format)

protection_level.description:
Key protection level.
Refer to the `Key.ProtectionLevel` enum for a description of values.

region.description: Region where the key is stored.

values.rsa_oaep_2048_sha256: RSA-OAEP (Optimal Asymmetric Encryption Padding) with a 2048-bit key and SHA-256 hash function
values.rsa_oaep_3072_sha256: RSA-OAEP (Optimal Asymmetric Encryption Padding) with a 3072-bit key and SHA-256 hash function (recommended)
values.rsa_oaep_4096_sha256: RSA-OAEP (Optimal Asymmetric Encryption Padding) with a 4096-bit key and SHA-256 hash function

values.ec_p256_sha256: ECDSA (Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm) on the P-256 Curve and SHA-256 hash function (recommended)
values.ec_p384_sha384: ECDSA (Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm) on the P-384 Curve and SHA-384 hash function
values.rsa_pss_2048_sha256: RSA-PSS (Probabilistic Signature Scheme) with a 2048-bit key and SHA-256 hash function
values.rsa_pss_3072_sha256: RSA-PSS (Probabilistic Signature Scheme) with a 3072-bit key and SHA-256 hash function
values.rsa_pss_4096_sha256: RSA-PSS (Probabilistic Signature Scheme) with a 4096-bit key and SHA-256 hash function
values.rsa_pkcs1_2048_sha256: RSA-PKCS1 (Public Key Cryptography Standards) with a 2048-bit key and SHA-256 hash function
values.rsa_pkcs1_3072_sha256: RSA-PKCS1 (Public Key Cryptography Standards) with a 3072-bit key and SHA-256 hash function
values.rsa_pkcs1_4096_sha256: RSA-PKCS1 (Public Key Cryptography Standards) with a 4096-bit key and SHA-256 hash function
values.ml_dsa_44: ML-DSA (Module-Lattice Digital Signature Algorithm) FIPS 204 post-quantum signature scheme with security category 2
values.ml_dsa_65: ML-DSA (Module-Lattice Digital Signature Algorithm) FIPS 204 post-quantum signature scheme with security category 3
values.ml_dsa_87: ML-DSA (Module-Lattice Digital Signature Algorithm) FIPS 204 post-quantum signature scheme with security category 5

values.ml_kem_768: ML-KEM (Module-Lattice Key Encapsulation Mechanism) FIPS 203 post-quantum KEM with security category 3 (recommended)
values.ml_kem_1024: ML-KEM (Module-Lattice Key Encapsulation Mechanism) FIPS 203 post-quantum KEM with security category 5

values.aes_256_gcm: 256-bit Advanced Encryption Standard (AES-256) keys in Galois Counter Mode (GCM)

values.scaleway_kms: Key Manager generates the key material upon key creation
values.external: Key Manager creates a key with key material coming from an external source

values.software: Cryptographic operations are performed in software
values.hsm: Cryptographic operations are performed within a dedicated Hardware Security Module (HSM)

rotation_period.description:
Rotation period.
Time interval between two key rotations. The minimum duration is 24 hours and the maximum duration is 1 year (876000 hours). (in seconds)

next_rotation_at.description:
Key next rotation date.
Timestamp indicating the next scheduled rotation. (RFC 3339 format)

values.enabled: The key can be used for cryptographic operations.
values.disabled: The key cannot be used for cryptographic operations.
values.pending_key_material: Key material must be imported before the key can be used for cryptographic operations.

symmetric_encryption.description:
Encrypt and decrypt arbitrary payloads using a symmetric encryption algorithm.
See the `Key.Algorithm.SymmetricEncryption` enum for a description of values.

asymmetric_encryption.description:
Encrypt and decrypt arbitrary payloads using an asymmetric encryption algorithm.
See the `Key.Algorithm.AsymmetricEncryption` enum for a description of values.

asymmetric_signing.description:
Sign and verify arbitrary messages using an asymmetric signing algorithm.
See the `Key.Algorithm.AsymmetricSigning` enum for a description of values.

key_encapsulation.description:
Wrap and unwrap key using a key encapsulation algorithm.
See the `Key.Algorithm.KeyEncapulation` enum for a description of values.

key_id.description: ID of the associated key. (UUID format)

index.description:
Index of the key rotation.
The rotation index tracks the specific version of the key material.

status.description:
Status of the key rotation.
See the `KeyRotation.Status` enum for a description of possible values.

manually_rotated.description: Returns `true` if the key was rotated manually, or `false` if it was rotated automatically by a rotation policy.

updated_at.description: Key rotation last modification date. (RFC 3339 format)

algorithms.description: Returns a list of algorithms matching the requested criteria.

rotations.description: Single page of key rotations matching the requested criteria.

total_count.description: Total count of key rotations matching the requested criteria.

keys.description: Single page of keys matching the requested criteria.

total_count.description: Total count of keys matching the requested criteria.

key_id.description: ID of the key used to generate the signature. (UUID format)
ID of the key used for verification. (UUID format)

valid.description:
Defines whether the signature is valid.
Returns `true` if the signature is valid for the digest and key, and `false` otherwise.

get.description: Lists all cryptographic algorithms supported by the Key Manager service.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region you want to target

parameters.name: usages
parameters.description: Filter by key usage.

get.description:
Retrieve a list of keys across all Projects in an Organization or within a specific Project.
If the user has permissions for all current and future projects: Either organization_id or project_id is required.
If the user has permissions for all current projects or only specific projects: The project_id is required.
The `region` parameter in path is needed in both case.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region you want to target

parameters.name: organization_id
parameters.description: (Optional) Filter by Organization ID. (UUID format)

parameters.name: project_id
parameters.description: (Optional) Filter by Project ID. (UUID format)

parameters.name: tags
parameters.description: (Optional) List of tags to filter on.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: (Optional) Filter by key name.

parameters.name: usage
parameters.description:
(Optional) Filter keys by usage.
Select from symmetric encryption, asymmetric encryption, asymmetric signing or key_encapsulation.

parameters.name: scheduled_for_deletion
parameters.description: Filter keys based on their deletion status. By default, only keys not scheduled for deletion are returned in the output.

parameters.name: protection_level
parameters.description:
(Optional) Filter keys by protection level.
Select from software or hsm.

post.description: Create a key in a given region specified by the `region` parameter. You can use keys to encrypt or decrypt arbitrary payloads, to sign and verify messages or to generate data encryption keys. **Data encryption keys are not stored in Key Manager**.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region you want to target

project_id.description: ID of the Project containing the key. (UUID format)

usage.description:
Key usage.
See the `Key.Usage` enum for a description of possible values.

rotation_policy.description:
(Optional) Rotation policy of the key.
If not specified, no rotation policy will be applied to the key.

unprotected.description:
(Optional) Defines whether key protection is applied to a key. Protected keys can be used but not deleted.
Default value is `false`.

origin.description:
Key origin.
Refer to the `Key.Origin` enum for a description of values.

protection_level.description:
Key Protection level.
Refer to the `Key.Protection` enum for a description of values.

get.description: Retrieve metadata for a specified key using the `region` and `key_id` parameters.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region you want to target

parameters.name: key_id
parameters.description: ID of the key to target. (UUID format)

patch.description: Modify a key's metadata including name, description and tags, specified by the `key_id` and `region` parameters.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region you want to target

parameters.name: key_id
parameters.description: ID of the key to update. (UUID format)

tags.description: (Optional) Updated list of the key's tags.

rotation_policy.description:
(Optional) Updated rotation policy of the key.
If not specified, the key's existing rotation policy applies.

delete.description: Permanently delete a key specified by the `region` and `key_id` parameters. This action is irreversible. Any data encrypted with this key, including data encryption keys, will no longer be decipherable.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region you want to target

parameters.name: key_id
parameters.description: ID of the key to delete. (UUID format)

post.description: Decrypt an encrypted payload using an existing key, specified by the `key_id` parameter. The maximum payload size that can be decrypted is equivalent to the encrypted output of 64 KB of data (around 131 KB).

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region you want to target

parameters.name: key_id
parameters.description:
ID of the key to decrypt with.
The key must have an usage set to `symmetric_encryption` or `asymmetric_encryption`. (UUID format)

ciphertext.description:
Ciphertext data to decrypt.
Data size must be between 1 and 131071 bytes.

associated_data.description:
(Optional) Additional authenticated data.
The additional data must match the value passed in the encryption request. Only supported by keys with a usage set to `symmetric_encryption`.

post.description: Delete previously imported key material. This renders the associated cryptographic key unusable for any operation. The key's origin must be `external`.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region you want to target

parameters.name: key_id
parameters.description: ID of the key of which to delete the key material. (UUID format)

key_rotation_index.description:
(Optional) Rotation index of which to delete the key material.
Default to latest rotation if not set.

post.description: Disable a given key, preventing it to be used for cryptographic operations. Disabling a key renders it unusable. You must specify the `region` and `key_id` parameters.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region you want to target

parameters.name: key_id
parameters.description: ID of the key to disable. (UUID format)

post.description: Enable a given key to be used for cryptographic operations. Enabling a key allows you to make a disabled key usable again. You must specify the `region` and `key_id` parameters.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region you want to target

parameters.name: key_id
parameters.description: ID of the key to enable. (UUID format)

post.description: Encrypt a payload using an existing key, specified by the `key_id` parameter. The maximum payload size that can be encrypted is 64 KB of plaintext.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region you want to target

parameters.name: key_id
parameters.description:
ID of the key to use for encryption.
The key must have an usage set to `symmetric_encryption` or `asymmetric_encryption`. (UUID format)

plaintext.description:
Plaintext data to encrypt.
Data size must be between 1 and 65535 bytes.

associated_data.description:
(Optional) Additional authenticated data.
Additional data which will not be encrypted, but authenticated and appended to the encrypted payload. Only supported by keys with a usage set to `symmetric_encryption`.

post.description:
Create a new data encryption key for cryptographic operations outside of Key Manager. The data encryption key is encrypted and must be decrypted using the key you have created in Key Manager.

The data encryption key is returned in plaintext and ciphertext but it should only be stored in its encrypted form (ciphertext). Key Manager does not store your data encryption key. To retrieve your key's plaintext, use the `Decrypt` method with your key's ID and ciphertext.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region you want to target

parameters.name: key_id
parameters.description: ID of the key. (UUID format)

algorithm.description:
Algorithm with which the data encryption key will be used to encrypt and decrypt arbitrary payloads.
See the `DataKey.Algorithm.SymmetricEncryption` enum for a description of values.

without_plaintext.description:
(Optional) Defines whether to return the data encryption key's plaintext in the response object.
Default value is `false`, meaning that the plaintext is returned.
Set it to `true` if you do not wish the plaintext to be returned in the response object.

post.description: Import externally generated key material into Key Manager to derive a new cryptographic key. The key's origin must be `external`.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region you want to target

parameters.name: key_id
parameters.description:
ID of the key in which to import key material.
The key's origin must be `external`. (UUID format)

key_material.description:
The key material.
Deprecated. Use `encrypted_key_material` instead. The key material is a random sequence of bytes used to derive a cryptographic key.

salt.description:
(Optional) Salt value to pass the key derivation function.
A salt is random data added to key material to ensure unique derived keys, even if the input is similar. It helps strengthen security when the key material has low randomness (low entropy).

encrypted_key_material.description:
The encrypted key material to import.
This material must be encrypted using the public key and the exact wrapping algorithm returned by the `GetKeyMaterialImportParameters` method.

post.description: Retrieve the cryptographic parameters (public key and import token) required to securely import key material into an existing key. The key's origin must be `external`.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region you want to target

parameters.name: key_id
parameters.description: ID of the key into which to import the key material. (UUID format)

wrapping_algorithm.description:
The wrapping algorithm the client will use to encrypt the key material.
Supported values are: `rsa_oaep_2048_sha256`, `rsa_oaep_3072_sha256`, `rsa_oaep_4096_sha256`.

post.description: Apply protection to a given key specified by the `key_id` parameter. Applying key protection means that your key can be used and modified, but it cannot be deleted.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region you want to target

parameters.name: key_id
parameters.description: ID of the key to apply key protection to. (UUID format)

get.summary: Get the public key in PEM format.
get.description: Retrieves the public portion of an asymmetric cryptographic key in PEM format.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region you want to target

parameters.name: key_id
parameters.description: ID of the key. (UUID format)

post.description: Restore a key and all its rotations scheduled for deletion specified by the `region` and `key_id` parameters.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region you want to target

post.description: Generate a new version of an existing key with new key material. Previous key versions remain usable to decrypt previously encrypted data, but the key's new version will be used for subsequent encryption operations and data key generation.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region you want to target

parameters.name: key_id
parameters.description: ID of the key to rotate. (UUID format)

get.description:
Retrieve a list of all rotations associated with a specific key.
The `key_id` and `region` parameters in the path are required.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region you want to target

parameters.name: key_id
parameters.description: ID of the key to list rotations for. (UUID format)

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
(Optional) Filter key rotations by their status.
See the `KeyRotation.Status` enum for a description of possible values.

post.description: Use a given key to sign a message digest. The key must have its usage set to `asymmetric_signing`. The digest must be created using the same digest algorithm that is defined in the key's algorithm configuration.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region you want to target

parameters.name: key_id
parameters.description: ID of the key to use for signing. (UUID format)

digest.description:
Pre-hashed digest of the message to sign.
For ECDSA and RSA keys, the digest generated using the key's hashing algorithm: 32 bytes (SHA-256) or 48 bytes (SHA-384).
The 64-byte bound only exists for the ML-DSA backward-compatibility case below.
Also accepted for ML-DSA for backward compatibility only; signatures may not conform to the ML-DSA spec, not recommended for new usage. Prefer `message` or `external_mu` for ML-DSA.

msg.description:
Full message to sign as-is.
Only supported for ML-DSA keys (`raw` signing): the server computes the μ message representative internally before signing. Between 1 and 4096 bytes.

external_mu.description:
ML-DSA pre-hashed μ message representative, exactly 64 bytes.
Must equal SHAKE256(tr ‖ 0x00 ‖ 0x00 ‖ message), where `tr` is the SHAKE256 of the key's public key. Signatures produced from other pre-hash computations (e.g. HashML-DSA) cannot be verified through this API.

post.description: Remove key protection from a given key specified by the `key_id` parameter. Removing key protection means that your key can be deleted anytime.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region you want to target

parameters.name: key_id
parameters.description: ID of the key to remove key protection from. (UUID format)

post.description: Unwrap (decrypt) a wrapped key using an existing key, specified by the `key_id` parameter. The key must use ML-KEM algorithm. The maximum key size that can be unwrapped is 4 KB of ciphertext.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region you want to target

post.description: Use a given key to verify a message signature against a message digest. The key must have its usage set to `asymmetric_signing`. The message digest must be generated using the same digest algorithm that is defined in the key's algorithm configuration.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region you want to target

parameters.name: key_id
parameters.description: ID of the key to use for signature verification. (UUID format)

digest.description:
Digest that was signed.
For ECDSA and RSA keys, the digest of the original message, generated using the key's hashing algorithm.

msg.description:
Message that was signed.
For ML-DSA keys, the full original message. This also verifies signatures made with `raw` or `external_mu`: send the message whose μ was signed, not the μ itself (a μ payload always fails). Messages over 4096 bytes cannot be verified through this endpoint.

post.description: Wrap (encrypt) a key using an existing key, specified by the `key_id` parameter. The key must use ML-KEM algorithm. The maximum key size that can be wrapped is 2 KB of plaintext.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region you want to target
